new: It is a small picture of a common bind: both sides do well if both cooperate, and each is tempted to cheat. Which ways of playing survive?
why: The page never says why anyone would care. One sentence is enough. It can be applied alongside everything in readable.json.

old: Cheating a cooperator pays 5, mutual cooperation 3, mutual defection 1.
new: If one player defects and the other cooperates, the defector gets 5 points and the cooperator gets [NUMBER]; when both cooperate each gets 3, and when both defect each gets 1.

old: A slip costs about three rounds to repair.
new: When one of them slips, it takes about three rounds for the pair to get back to cooperating. All the machine keeps track of is where it is in this routine: waiting for a first defection, waiting for a second, or cooperating. Those three places are called its states, and that is what is meant below by a machine of three states.
why: "States" is used six times on the page and in the fourth game of the strip, and is never explained. This is the one addition I would most like to see. Use instead of R13.
needs: Confirm against the machine's table (the small print of the opening picture gives state 0: defect, state 1: defect, state 2: cooperate) that these are its three states and that "the place it is in its routine" is a fair account of a state.

old: Set the slips to nothing and wait: cooperation arrives in brief spikes and is eaten each time. Set them to between 1% and 3%, with long games, and after a while a kind that opens with two thorns tends to take the bed and hold it. It can take tens of thousands of generations for anything to happen, and that is part of the result.
new: You can open the bed and try it. It starts running by itself, with 3% of moves slipping and long games. Wait, and after a while a kind of machine whose plant begins with two thorns tends to take over the bed and hold it. That can take tens of thousands of generations, which the page gets through in [HOW LONG BY THE CLOCK]. Then set the slips to nothing: cooperation arrives in brief spikes and is lost again each time. [WHY THE LONG WAIT IS PART OF THE RESULT, IN ONE SENTENCE, OR NOTHING.]
why: The live page already starts at 3% slips and long games, so the stranger meets the second experiment first; and "tens of thousands of generations" sounds like an afternoon when it is seconds. Use instead of R06, R07 and R08.
needs: Three things. (a) That the live page opens running, at 3% slips and games of 50 rounds on average: I saw this, but it is not in the story. (b) How long tens of thousands of generations take on an ordinary computer: in a headless browser I saw about 5,000 generations a second; the first take-over came after about 4 seconds on one visit and had not come after 12 on another. (c) Why the wait "is part of the result".

old: They went through every machine with up to three states, tested each as an equilibrium against all possible strategies when moves are noisy, and singled this one out.
new: They went through every machine with up to three states, asked of each whether any possible way of playing could gain against it when [MOVES CAN SLIP, or PLAYERS CAN MISREAD EACH OTHER'S MOVES], and singled this one out.
why: Says in plain words what "tested as an equilibrium" means, in the words you use for your own test lower down ("gain ... against the machine"). Use instead of R25.
needs: Two things. (a) That their test is the one you describe as your own: whether anything can gain against the machine. (b) What is noisy in their paper. Your sources give its title as about "private monitoring", which suggests that what goes wrong there is what each player sees of the other's move, not the move itself. If so, "when moves are noisy" is loosely put even now, and "slips" would be wrong.

old: That a little noise can help cooperation in small populations.
new: That a few slips can help cooperation in small populations.

needs: Whether the "noise" of Miller (1996) and the "errors" of Zhang (2018) are slips as on this page (a player does the other thing) or mistakes in what a player sees of the other's move. If the latter, keep a looser word, for instance "a few mistakes", which also matches the line above it.
